concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa, consistent with neutrophilic panniculitis.
The patient has a history of sickle cell disease and presented with severe intermittent abdominal pain, which is a common symptom of a sickle cell crisis.
The patient has a history of ulcerative colitis and presented with bloody stools, which is a common symptom of an ulcerative colitis flare.
The patient has a history of autoimmune hepatitis and presented with elevated C-reactive protein levels, which is a common indicator of an autoimmune hepatitis flare.

rationales.F04: Abdominal pain can be associated with sickle cell crisis, ulcerative colitis flare, or autoimmune hepatitis flare.
rationales.F05: Bloody stools are more commonly associated with ulcerative colitis flare.
rationales.F06: Sickle cell disease is a strong indicator of sickle cell crisis.
rationales.F07: Ulcerative colitis is a strong indicator of ulcerative colitis flare.
rationales.F08: Autoimmune hepatitis is a strong indicator of autoimmune hepatitis flare.
rationales.F09: Hemorrhagic vesicles are a distinctive feature of neutrophilic panniculitis.
rationales.F11: Elevated C-reactive protein level is a marker of inflammation, which can be seen in neutrophilic panniculitis, sickle cell crisis, ulcerative colitis flare, or autoimmune hepatitis flare.
rationales.F12: Leukocytosis is a marker of inflammation, which can be seen in neutrophilic panniculitis, sickle cell crisis, ulcerative colitis flare, or autoimmune hepatitis flare.
